stories.notes: Story has empty acceptance criteria and null spec — blank slate requiring full elaboration. Live preview across GO, UP, MX platforms is complex: needs requirement elaboration (openspec first) to define ACs and technical depth around real-time preview mechanics, then hardening (speckit) for testability, edge cases (sync failures, concurrent edits, cross-platform rendering), and security (preview token validation, content injection).

agentContributions.notes: Novel capability — live preview does not exist in the codebase. The single integration point is useContent (236+ consumers), which funnels all Contentstack content via getContentByKey. Every Contentstack component (ContentstackLink, ContentstackImage, ContentstackTable, ContentstackContentCards, etc.) inherits from this hook, so preview behavior propagates without per-component changes. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time; VCs are written to the boundary of our code.

Openspec provided an empty AC list but valuable architectural context: useContent is the single integration point with 236+ consumers, and all Contentstack components inherit preview behavior through it. I built the full AC set from scratch based on the story title, file paths, and that context. CAVEAT: Without the actual file contents of useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx, etc., I inferred the Contentstack Live Preview SDK contract from the story title and standard Contentstack live-preview patterns. Specifics about the wire protocol, initialization sequence, and data shape may need adjustment once the implementation team reviews the SDK documentation. AC-7 and AC-8 address the critical security concern that draft content must never leak into caches or SSR output. AC-9 addresses accessibility. AC-4/5/6/11 cover error handling and resilience. AC-10 covers nested content, a common edge case with Contentstack references. AC-12 covers the new-draft-entry edge case. AC-13 covers navigation persistence.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Both agents contributed non-overlapping value: openspec identified the critical integration point (useContent hook, 236+ consumers, boundary-testing constraint) and speckit constructed a comprehensive 13-AC set covering security (AC-7/8 cache/SSR leak prevention), error resilience (AC-4/5/6/11), accessibility (AC-9), and edge cases (AC-10 nested references, AC-12 new-draft-entry, AC-13 navigation persistence). However, speckit explicitly caveated that it inferred the Contentstack Live Preview SDK contract from the story title and standard patterns without reviewing actual source files (useContent.ts, ContentstackContext.tsx). The wire protocol, initialization sequence, and data shape assumptions in the ACs may not match the real SDK API. A human reviewer with access to the Contentstack SDK documentation and the codebase should validate the ACs before implementation begins.
